name: desire for social contact
description: A desire to experience an interaction with a person or animal.
perceptions: It's been a while since I've interacted with people.
Friendly social contact would feel nice.

guidance.description: Ways To Get Some Quick Social Contact When You're Feeling Really Lonely And Isolated: meetups, religious service, family, friends, online chat, support group, counselor. Know there's nothing shameful about wanting social contact. It's a basic human need.

variations.name: desire for companionship
variations.description: Wanting for meaningful social interaction with a person or group that knows and accepts you.
perceptions: I'd like to be amongst people I know and am comfortable with.

comparisons.description: 'Desire for social contact' is more general - anyone with a pulse will do -- even just being around strangers in the food court. A 'desire for companionship' is more specific, wanting to be around people who know something about you.

variations.name: desire for pair bond
variations.description: A desire to find a person to share your life with.
perceptions: I need to find my life partner.

variations.name: desire to be around animals
variations.description: A desire for interactions with animals. These can be simple and satisfying relationships.
perceptions: I'd like to spend some time with animals.
They aren't going to judge me for what I say, how I look, or what I believe.
They reconnect me with nature in a way.

guidance.description: Some of the greatest moments in life include the day we met our pets for the first time, and the day we adopted them and they came home with us. Here are 10 things to consider before bringing a new dog or cat home.

variations.name: desire for any attention
variations.description: A deep need for any kind of social attention, even negative attention.
perceptions: I'm so ready for social attention that even negative attention is better than none.
Being naughty will get me some attention.

guidance.description: If you or someone you know seeks attention to the point of being annoying, here are some resources that may be of interest.

examples: A kid crying on the playground to get sympathy.

comparisons.description: Being 'weird' on purpose to attract attention is a specific kind of attention-seeking.
Feeling lonely would certainly drive a desire for social contact, but you can desire social interaction for the stimulation without necessarily feeling lonely.

You might just want to hang out with people without trying to influence them in any way or engage in any kind of status re-evaluation. Likewise, if you do want to influence someone, it could be for reasons other than social status like safety, parenting, etc.

commentaries.quote: Man is, by nature, a social animal.

Human beings are social creatures. We are social not just in the trivial sense that we like company, and not just in the obvious sense that we each depend on others. We are social in a more elemental way: simply to exist as a normal human being requires interaction with other people.

Humans have evolved the basic need for social connection because it is vital to our survival. This need is rooted deep within us biologically. And we have even developed an evolutionary warning signal that tells us when our need for connection is not met.
No one appreciates the very special genius of your conversation as the dog does.

Attention seeking behaviors can take many forms. It can be an individual constantly talking, seeking validation, making noises, raising a hand, clowning around, blurting out the need for someone to help, teach or watch them do something; tattling, provoking a confrontation, incessantly questioning, bullying or teasing, fishing for compliments, being argumentative, and telling fantastical stories or exaggerated unrealistic experiences.

Don't kid yourself that provocative behavior is always 'resisting social pressure'. Most of the time, it's just a different interpretation for how to position your identity against the social background. Few people would do stupid, expensive, painful, inconvenient things were it not driven as a reaction to social pressure.
